summary: Gavin D'Costa works in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Bedford Modern School, the University of Cambridge, and the University of Birmingham under John Hick. His career includes posts at Bristol, Pontifical Gregorian University, and the Pontifical University of Saint Thomas Aquinas.

Gavin Flood is an indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Lancaster University under Andrew Rawlinson and David Smith. He held positions at the University of Wales, Lampeter, the University of Stirling, Oxford, Campion Hall, and Yale-NUS College.

Gaya Charan Tripathi is an indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Ulrich Schneider from around 1963 to 1966. He served as Principal of Ganganatha Jha Kendriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha from circa 1977 to 1999.
Geetha K. Wilson is an Indology scholar who is attested in 2026 as a doctoral student under Claire Maes and as a faculty member at the University of Tübingen.
Geir Heierstad is an Indology scholar who served as Director at Oslo Metropolitan University in 2014 and is attested as a faculty member at the University of Oslo in 2026.

Gelek is a Tibetologist who served as a researcher at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 1998). He has also held appointments as a visiting lecturer at the University of California and a visiting scholar at the University of Oxford.

Gelek Rimpoche (1939–2017) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. Educated at Drepung Monastery, Young Lamas Home School, and Cornell, he directed Tibet House in New Delhi in 1965 and founded Jewel Heart in 1988.

Gembo Dorji is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed studies at Tango Buddhist College, the East-West Center, and the University of Tokyo, training under traditional teachers including Tenzin Dhendrup, Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima, and Trulku Jigme Choedra.

Gen'ichi Yamazaki (1935–2015) was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He earned his degrees from the University of Tokyo, served as a researcher at Toyo Bunko (circa 1962–1975), and was a professor at Kokugakuin University in 2006.

Gendun Chopel (1903–1951) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Drisha, Kumbum, Labrang, and Drepung Monasteries under teachers including Gendun Tendzin Gyatso and Sherab Gyatso.
Gendun Chophel (1903–1951) was an active figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sherab Gyatso from around 1927 to 1934 and held a post at the Maha Bodhi Society in 1941.
Gendun Rinpoche (1918–1997) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master. He founded several centres, including Dhagpo Kagyu Ling, where he served as abbot and retreat master from circa 1977 to 1997.

Genjun Sasaki (1915–1999) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar educated at Kyoto University under multiple scholars. He held professorships at Otani University, visited Hamburg as a guest professor in 1956, and taught at Harvard and Osaka University.
Genro (1717–1789) was a figure in Buddhist studies who succeeded Hakuin Ekaku and held the position of za (first seat) at Myoshin-ji.
Genryu Kagoshima (1912–2001) was a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Komazawa University from around 1932 to 1937 and later served as a professor there from circa 1957 to 1983.

Gensho Imanari (1925–2020) was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He earned his degrees, including a PhD, from Waseda University, served as an assistant professor at Kokushikan University, and became professor emeritus at Rissho University.
Genshu Watanabe (1869–1963) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied at Toyo University and was a dharma heir of Sogaku Harada.

Genzao (died 1993) was a practitioner and scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Dzogchen Monastery until 1950 and trained under traditional teachers Jiangze Rinpoche and Kalu Rinpoche.

Geo Widengren (1907–1996) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies, studying under Henrik Samuel Nyberg at Stockholm and Uppsala. He was Dean at Uppsala University (1937–1973) and served as Vice President and President of the IAHR.

Geoff Childs is a scholar of Tibetology and anthropology/history. He earned his PhD at Indiana University Bloomington in 1998 under Tsetan Chonjore, held a postdoctoral fellowship at the Australian National University, and joined Washington University in St. Louis in 2002.
